I list a minimal externally-SIGKILLed checkpoint set (A1–A2, L1–L6, R1–R3, plus a duplicate-incarnation takeover) with the expected irreversible state at each. Three P0 issues beyond the matrix itself: the post-consumption/pre-`child.release()` window is untested across a real process death and is the sharpest second-user-launch hazard; `accept()`'s unconditional `released=1` lets a coordinator-initiated release free local admission capacity while the lease row stays `granted` and the cgroup stays populated; and the two named gaps (remove-before-Seal, create-before-boundary-commit) are correctly permanently-uncertain but escalate through `MAX_ACTIVE`/headroom into installation-wide refusal of new obligations. Those gaps are liveness-only and should not block MR3, provided they are pinned by tests, documented as permanent, and given a separately-owned authenticated-clearance recovery path; neither path absence nor a generation change is admissible as resolution. Also flagged: the fixture's `reply()` bypasses reply authentication (cheap fix that strengthens the whole compositional argument), the existing fault hooks are `cfg(test)`/thread-local and cannot drive an out-of-process daemon, and the hardcoded socket plus process-wide env overrides will collide across isolated daemons.
